text:
alex: Quick question — we keep hitting ambiguity in the matcher when host wildcards + path segment globs overlap. proposing a deterministic tie-break order so runtime doesn't make surprising picks. thoughts?

maria: +1 we need something predictable. current behavior feels like whichever route was created earlier wins and that's causing bugs. :grimacing:

jun: can you sketch the rules you'd want?
alex: sketch below. aim: simple, leans toward developer intent (more specific wins), but allows explicit overrides. rough order: 1) exact host literal > host wildcard count (fewer wildcards wins) 2) path specificity (count static segments, then fewer globs) 3) header constraints matched (more matches wins) 4) explicit priority field if set 5) creation time fallback.
simon: sounds sensible. do we treat `*.example.com` vs `api.*.example.com` purely by wildcard count or by label specificity?
alex: prefer label specificity: compare number of host labels matched literally from left-to-right starting at TLD side. eg `api.example.com` > `*.example.com` > `*.example.*` etc. fewer wildcard labels => more specific. also handle leading wildcard vs mid-label wildcard same rule.
tasha: ok but path specificity is tricky: `/v1/users/*` vs `/v1/:id/profile` (we support named params). how to rank named params vs `*` vs regex?
jun: propose ordering for path segments: literal segment > named param (":id") > single-segment wildcard ("+") > multi-segment glob ("*") > regex (explicit if used, counted as least specific unless anchored). That matches typical frameworks.
maria: can we add a small example block in the doc so PMs / SDK folks can reason about it?
alex: sure, quick examples:```
# routes in order of declaration (but ordering shouldn't matter after tie-break):
route A: host = "api.redwood.com", path = "/v1/users/:id"
route B: host = "*.redwood.com", path = "/v1/users/*"
route C: host = "api.redwood.com", path = "/v1/users/*", headers = {"x-beta": "true"}

# matching: request host api.redwood.com, path /v1/users/123, no headers -> A wins (exact host + literal+named param)
# request host api.redwood.com, path /v1/users/123, header x-beta=true -> C wins (header constraint more specific)
# request host foo.redwood.com, path /v1/users/abc -> B wins (host wildcard matches)
```
simon: nice. about header constraints — count only exact matches, not presence checks, right?
alex: yes. scoring: each exact header=value match adds +1. presence-only constraints add +0.5. these are just tie-break weights applied after host/path ranking.
tasha: what about negative matches (x-env != staging) and regex header values? treat them as less specific than exact eq?
jun: negative matches should be considered less specific (used for exclusions), so they count lower. regex header matches count similar to presence but flagged as expensive; we prefer explicit eq > regex > negative.
maria: where do explicit `priority` or `weight` fields come in? team might want to just force a route to win.
alex: explicit `priority` (integer, higher wins) should be last determinative before creation time but will override header/path scoring. i.e., if two routes are otherwise equal, check priority. we should require a warning in console when someone sets priority to avoid misuse.
simon: runtime: do we want to compute a composite score per route and pick max? cheaper to evaluate if we short-circuit by host first etc.
jun: implement staged checks: filter by host candidates (fast index), then compute path specificity score, then header score, then priority. avoid evaluating expensive regexes until necessary.
ops-bot: deploy-check: matcher change is a behavioral change. need migration plan + tests. create canary with sample config and verify traffic.
maria: agree. also update rule docs + SDK route validator to warn about shadowed routes.
tasha: one UX ask: in console show the matching score breakdown for a request (host 8/10, path 6/10, headers 2/10, final priority = 16) — helps debug.
alex: good idea. I'll draft a PR with RFC text + example unit tests. action: alex to open RFC, jun to review runtime perf implications, maria to update console mockups.
simon: ack. +1 to RFC.
alex: thanks — will ping when PR is up. :thumbsup:
